newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end down on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end down on low demand.

text.p: Pakistan's money rates closed lower on Monday amid low borrowing demand and an inflow of 5.2 billion rupees on maturity of three-year Federal Investment Bonds (FIBs), dealers said.
They said rates were likely to remain low on Tuesday as the market had closed seven billion rupees in surplus.
"The overnight market traded in the range of one to two percent," a dealer at Standard Chartered Bank said. Lenders were looking for bids but no major borrowing interest was seen.
